description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Heat Transfer topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: heat-transfer

facts.claim: Conduction, convection and radiation

source.quote: Heat transfer is classified into various mechanisms, such as thermal conduction, thermal convection, thermal radiation

facts.claim: Radiation needs no medium (travels through vacuum)

source.quote: Thermal radiation occurs through a vacuum or any transparent medium

facts.claim: Heat flux is proportional to the negative temperature gradient

source.quote: the rate of heat transfer through a material is proportional to the negative gradient in the

facts.claim: Heat flow ~ current, temperature difference ~ voltage (thermal circuits)

source.quote: The heat flow can be modelled by analogy to an electrical circuit where heat flow is represented by current, temperatures are represented by voltages

facts.claim: Thermal resistance in K/W

source.quote: It is measured in units of kelvins per watt (K/W)

facts.claim: Fins extend the surface area to increase heat transfer

source.quote: fins are surfaces that extend from an object to increase the rate of heat transfer to or from the environment by increasing convection

facts.claim: Biot number = internal conduction resistance / surface convection resistance

source.quote: Bi is defined as the ratio of the conductive heat resistance within the object to the convective heat transfer resistance

facts.claim: Small Bi (< 0.1) allows the lumped model; temperature approaches the bath exponentially

source.quote: an exponential approach of the object temperature to the bath temperature

facts.claim: Fluid motion driven by an external source (pump, fan)

source.quote: fluid motion is generated by an external source (like a pump, fan, suction device, etc.)

facts.claim: Driven by density differences (buoyancy) from heating

source.quote: convection due to the effects of thermal expansion (change in density) and gravity/buoyancy can be assumed

facts.claim: Emitted power ∝ T⁴ (Stefan–Boltzmann)

source.quote: The proportionality to the fourth power of the absolute temperature

facts.claim: A black body has emissivity 1; real surfaces emit less

source.quote: An emissivity of one corresponds to a black body

facts.claim: View factor: fraction of radiation leaving one surface that reaches another

source.quote: is the proportion of the radiation which leaves surface

facts.claim: All radiation leaving a surface goes somewhere (factors sum to 1)

source.quote: Radiation leaving a surface within an enclosure is conserved

facts.claim: The log mean temperature difference (LMTD)

source.quote: In most simple systems this is the "log mean temperature difference" (LMTD)

facts.claim: Counter-flow is the most efficient arrangement

source.quote: The counter current design is the most efficient

facts.claim: Effectiveness = actual / maximum possible heat transfer

source.quote: we need to find the maximum possible heat transfer that can be hypothetically achieved

facts.claim: Used when outlet temperatures are not known (LMTD needs them)

source.quote: if the fluid inlet and outlet temperatures are specified or can be determined by simple energy balance, the LMTD method can be used

facts.claim: Boiling: liquid to vapour when vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure

source.quote: the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the pressure exerted on the liquid by the surrounding atmosphere

facts.claim: Diffusive flux ∝ concentration gradient (Fick's first law)

source.quote: Movement of particles from high to low concentration (diffusive flux) is directly proportional to the particle's concentration gradient
